description: The flagged lists the sealed second-call bodies carry, per row, for one tier. Each is the first answer's ungrounded units under src/complete/flagging.py, the frozen operational implementation, computed against the FIRST-PASS context. The bodies themselves carry the augmented context. Committed so a reviewer can rebuild every body exactly from committed files with no key.

population.rule: src.complete.augment.augment reports triggered; a row it does not fire on receives no second call and its layer answer is its first-pass answer.

grading_note: Nothing here is graded. No claim unit is scored and no rate is computed. The grading of record is a separate commit over committed files, per CLAUDE.md Rule 9.

flagged_units: For law-enforcement high-risk AI systems (Annex III points 1, 6 and 7 in the areas of law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control management), the testing is registered in the secure non-public section of the EU database under Article 49(4), point (d), with the information specified therein — not with the Annex IX information.
Therefore Annex IX points do not apply to the registration of such law-enforcement systems.
The technical documentation (Annex IV) must include the post-market monitoring plan.

Under Article 72(3), the post-market monitoring plan is part of the technical documentation referred to in Annex IV, and it underpins the post-market monitoring system that actively and systematically collects, documents, and analyses data on the high-risk AI system's performance throughout its lifetime to evaluate its continuous compliance with the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2.
Under Article 36(2), extensions of the scope of a notification follow the procedures in Articles 29 and 30.
Accordingly, per Article 29(2), the application must be accompanied by:
an accreditation certificate (where one exists) from a national accreditation body attesting compliance with Article 31; and
any valid documents related to existing designations under other Union harmonisation legislation.
Where no accreditation certificate can be provided, the body must instead supply all documentary evidence necessary to verify, recognise and monitor its compliance with Article 31.
However, the provided context does not list which specific actors those are.
By putting its trademark on the system, the distributor is considered a provider (Article 25(1)(a)) and assumes the provider's obligations under Article 16.
As a provider, it must have a post-market monitoring system in place.

Because affixing the CE marking in a way that violates Article 48 constitutes formal non-compliance under Article 83(1)(a), the market surveillance authority must require the provider to put an end to the non-compliance within a period it may prescribe.
If the non-compliance persists, the authority must take appropriate and proportionate measures to restrict or prohibit the system on the market, or ensure it is recalled or withdrawn without delay.
The offences listed in Annex II are:

The EU AI Act applies from 2 August 2026, with certain exceptions (Chapters I and II from 2 February 2025; specified provisions from 2 August 2025; and Article 6(1) with corresponding obligations from 2 August 2027).
Before putting into service a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III (except point 2), a deploying public authority must:

Perform a fundamental rights impact assessment covering the elements listed in Article 27(1) (as a body governed by public law), and once performed, notify the market surveillance authority of its results using the required template (Article 27(3)).
For systems in the areas of law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control management, the registration must be made in a secure non-public section of the database (Article 49(4)).
Providers must grant market surveillance authorities:

**Full access** to the documentation and the training, validation and testing data sets used for developing high-risk AI systems—where relevant and limited to what is necessary, including through APIs or other remote-access technical means (Art. 74(12)).
In the case of an SME, including a start-up, each fine shall be up to the percentages or amount referred to in the relevant paragraphs, whichever is lower.
Per MANAGE 3.1, an organisation must regularly monitor AI risks and benefits from third-party resources, and apply and document risk controls.
Transparency answers "what happened," explainability answers "how" a decision was made, and interpretability answers "why" a decision was made and its meaning or context to the user.
It requires:
Ensuring evaluations that use human subjects or their data reflect the population within the context of use, since non-representative data can lead to inaccurate assessments or harmful outcomes.
